name: bluebird-promisifyall-multiargs-oose-sdk
behavioral_change: In bluebird v_new (3.0.0), `Promise.promisify` and `Promise.promisifyAll` by default resolve the promise with only the first success value passed to the node-style callback, whereas v_old (2.x) collected multiple success values into an array. The call form is unchanged and no exception is raised by the library itself; the old array behaviour is restored with the new `multiArgs: true` option.
downstream_effect: oose-sdk's `extendRequest` in helpers/api.js promisifies a `request` instance with `P.promisifyAll(req)` and callers consume `postAsync` results with `.spread(res, body)`; after the upgrade the promise resolves to the bare response and 15 tests fail with `TypeError: expecting an array or an iterable object`. Stack frames name helpers/Prism.js and bluebird and request internals, but never helpers/api.js line 157 where the fix goes, and promisify or spread never appear in the output.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes one line in helpers/api.js, adding `{multiArgs: true}` to the `P.promisifyAll(req)` call in `extendRequest`.
documented_in: bluebird's "New in bluebird 3.0" document (docs/docs/new-in-bluebird-3.md, tag v3.7.2), section Promisification API changes, states in prose that promisification now uses only the first callback argument and that a new boolean option `multiArgs` restores the array behaviour. The document gives only prose for this change and no code for the `multiArgs` form; the downstream maintainer's later commit 2d8b31e applied the same fix.
failing_tests: 15 failing tests, listed in pinned/STATE-NEW.log; for example: mock should log out
